Among approved applicants, most had no negative balance, and an overdrawn account is a warning sign of cash-flow strain. This factor pushed your result most strongly toward bad credit. Two other important factors worked in your favor, but they were not enough to overcome it. Your proposed installment payment as a share of disposable income is 2.00%, below the approved average of about 3%, meaning your repayment burden is relatively light. Your requested loan term is 12 months, shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, which normally reduces risk because you repay faster. So the denial is driven mainly by the overdrawn account, not by the loan size or term. Next, focus on bringing your checking account back to a positive, stable balance for several months, avoid overdrafts, and build savings. Then ask the bank to reconsider or reapply once your account history shows reliable cash management. You may also ask whether a guarantor or co-applicant would help.
